verdict.text: Both findings sent back are fixed and nothing around them regressed.
The status version-mismatch problem now names `kmctl plugin update --harness <list>`, which is tested for both harnesses, and the antigravity.py docstring no longer mentions a doctor command.
The gates and all nine eval rows pass on my own stamp.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree with scratch HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME.
lint, format, tests and integration passed, and rows r1 to r9 passed: "stamp green: cf01df9041544b10cd2955ac042c187a9f1991f15e413e665d1d47896b8ad05c".
The state commit was deferred only because the scratch HOME has no git identity.
src/kmctl/plugin.py lines 1003-1008: the mismatch line now ends `run kmctl plugin update --harness {','.join(harnesses)}{suffix}`.
The changed-Claude-hook line still says plain `kmctl plugin update`.
That is correct because it only appears when claude is checked and update defaults to claude, and the docs say exactly this.
tests/test_antigravity.py test_status_version_mismatch_names_the_harness rewrites the lock ref and asserts that the problem ends with `--harness antigravity`.
It would fail on the old string.
tests/test_plugin.py line 942 now expects `--harness claude` at the end.

docs/reference/commands.md, the `kmctl plugin status` section: it now says that an older package names `kmctl plugin update --harness HARNESS` and a changed Claude hook names `kmctl plugin update`, which matches the code.
src/kmctl/antigravity.py module docstring: it now says `kmctl plugin status` uses the comparison and that any other check can call it.
The fix is at src/kmctl/plugin.py:1004-1008, with a test in tests/test_antigravity.py and an updated expectation in tests/test_plugin.py.
